answer: Agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each participant to lock a scarce, transferable stake before receiving any influence. When several identities coordinate to fake independent demand, a shared challenge can expose their common control; proven duplicates lose part of that stake, while honest agents keep theirs. The attacker must therefore buy and risk real capital for every fabricated identity, and repeated attempts deepen the loss spiral. Even on a tundra market ledge with few observers, this raises the cost of manufacturing influence rather than merely counting accounts.
